newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Berlusconi says pact with govt unlikely.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Berlusconi says pact with govt unlikely.

text.p: Italian opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi said on Tuesday that he saw little likelihood of reaching an agreement with the government over financial measures to help Italy into the single European currency.

Berlusconi had told reporters at the weekend that his opposition might be prepared to help Prodi with a mini-budget needed to bring Italy's deficit down to levels that would enable the country to meet single currency requirements.
On Tuesday, in a television interview, Berlusconi said he still believed such an agreement would be "useful."
But he added it would be "difficult for it to happen, because the left has come to power after 50 years and has no intention of sharing it."

Berlusconi repeated that his centre-right Freedom Alliance was willing to "do its bit if the government changes gear with the coming mini-budget and the 1998 budget and instead of new one-off hikes produces structural spending cuts."

The comments were aimed particularly at the hard-left Communist Refoundation party of Fausto Bertinotti, which holds the balance of power in the lower house of parliament and opposes any cuts in public spending or tax hikes.
Refoundation is unhappy over the new mini-budget and has threatened to withdraw its support if the government cuts a deal with the opposition.
The budget package is due to be unveiled in the coming weeks and is expected to contain 10-15 trillion lire of deficit cutting measures. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
